reason: The text portrays regular people with significant moral complexity and some unfavorable characterizations. While Isaac and Rebekah are shown piously seeking God's will, Esau is explicitly portrayed negatively—he 'despised his birthright' (וַיִּ֥בֶז עֵשָׂ֖ו אֶת־ הַבְּכֹרָֽה) and acts impulsively. Jacob, though described as 'tam' (complete/upright), is depicted manipulating his hungry, exhausted brother into surrendering his birthright through cunning negotiation. The narrative presents regular people as morally flawed actors, not uniformly favorable characters.
